sentences.text:
(Harisingh s/o Bhagwan Singh v/s State of Madhya Pradesh and another)
Indore, Dated : 13.08.2019 :-

Shri Rishi Raj Trivedi, learned counsel for the
applicant - Harisingh.

Shri Arvind Yadav, learned Public Prosecutor for
the Respondent/State.
Submissions were to be made on application for suspension of sentence which is I.A.No.2608/2019.

The applicant was earlier convicted for committing offence under Section 7 (I) read with Section 16 (i ) (A) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 by Judicial Magistrate, First Class,
Indore in Criminal Case No.767/2004 vide judgment dated 25.01.2017 and was sentenced to undergo 6 months RI and fine of Rs.1,000-00, in default to suffer 2 months additional RI.

This judgment was subjected to appeal and the appellate Court i.e. Special Judge [SC & ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act], Indore in Criminal appeal No.123/2017 vide judgment dated 17.11.2017 has dismissed the appeal and affirmed the sentence.

entities.text: Special Judge [SC & ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act], Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Against the appellate Court's order, this criminal revision was filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that he instead of making submissions on application for suspension of sentence would make final submissions in this matter.
The prayer is allowed.

Learned counsel submits that he does not seek to challenge the conclusion pertaining to the conviction and further submits that the applicant has since completed term of imprisonment of 6 months already and, therefore, the -: 2 :- Criminal Revision No.1707 of 2019.
period of sentence having been completed, this criminal revision be disposed of in above terms.
This prayer is also allowed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of revisional Court's record shows that on 17.11.2017 when the judgment was declared, the applicant was not present before the Court and non-bailable warrant was issued and the applicant was subsequently arrested on 15.03.2019.
He would have completed 6 months in jail on 18.09.2019.
However, a perusal of Certificate under Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure shows that he was in jail for 34 days as an under trial prisoner.
Looking to this period, the applicant has already completed 6 months imprisonment in the jail.
Consequently it is observed that applicant having completed 6 months RI in jail, the sentence imposed upon him of 6 months jail has already been completed.
The applicant shall be released from jail on depositing fine amount of Rs.1,000-00, if not already deposited.
With this, the criminal revision stands disposed of finally in the above terms.
A copy of this order be sent to the Trial Court along with the records for due compliance.
